description.text: Essential Utilities, Inc., referred to as “Essential Utilities”, “Essential”, the “Company”, “we”, “us”, or “our”, a Pennsylvania corporation, is the holding company for regulated utilities providing water, wastewater, or natural gas services to an estimated 5.5 million people in Pennsylvania, Ohio, Texas, Illinois, North Carolina, New Jersey, Indiana, Virginia, and Kentucky under the Aqua and Peoples brands. One of our largest operating subsidiaries, Aqua Pennsylvania, Inc., or Aqua Pennsylvania, accounted for approximately 57% of operating revenues and approximately 72% of income for our Regulated Water segment in 2025. As of December 31, 2025, Aqua Pennsylvania provided water or wastewater services to approximately one-half of the total number of water and wastewater customers we serve. Aqua Pennsylvania’s service territory is located in the suburban areas in counties north and west of the City of Philadelphia and in 28 other counties in Pennsylvania. Our other regulated water or wastewater utility subsidiaries provide similar services in seven additional states. Our Peoples subsidiaries provide natural gas service to approximately 747,000 customers in western Pennsylvania and Kentucky. Approximately 95% of the total number of natural gas utility customers we serve are in western Pennsylvania.

about.description_short: Essential Utilities, Inc. (NYSE: WTRG) delivers safe, clean, reliable services that improve quality of life for individuals, families, and entire communities. With a focus on water, wastewater and natural gas, Essential is committed to sustainable growth, operational excellence, a superior customer experience, and premier employer status. We are advocates for the communities we serve and are dedicated stewards of natural lands, protecting thousands of acres of forests and other habitats throughout our footprint. Operating as the Aqua and Peoples brands, Essential serves approximately 5.5 million people across nine states.

analysis_md:
# WTRG — Essential Utilities, Inc.
Engine 5.4.0 run, 2026-10-18. In scope (market cap $11.458B at $40.83, nasdaq_quote_api — under the $40B cutoff).

All figures below are copied from key_numbers.md, dcf_numbers.json, ttm.json, fundamentals.json, or the cited filing — none are recomputed.

## What it is
Regulated water, wastewater and natural gas utility (Aqua and Peoples brands), serving approximately 5.5 million people across nine states. Revenue is set by state utility commissions: the company spends on infrastructure, the spend enters rate base, and rates are set to recover it plus an allowed return. Q2 2026 (reported 2026-08-05): revenue $530.9M, +3.1% YoY, with regulated water revenue +7.6% on regulatory recoveries and volume; GAAP EPS $0.37, adjusted EPS $0.38, with merger-related costs weighing on GAAP. Management reaffirmed a 5%–7% EPS growth outlook and a $1.7B 2026 infrastructure-spending plan, and the quarterly dividend was raised 5.25% to $0.3606/share (payable 2026-09-01).

**The dominant fact is the pending merger.** On 2025-10-27 American Water Works (AWK) and Essential Utilities announced an all-stock merger: WTRG shareholders receive 0.305 AWK shares per WTRG share (≈10% premium at announcement), creating a combined company with ~$40B pro forma market value serving 4.7M+ water/wastewater and 740,000+ gas connections. Shareholders of both companies approved in February 2026; Kentucky (2026-04-21), Ohio (2026-05-14) and Virginia (2026-06-22) commissions have approved; a non-unanimous Pennsylvania settlement was filed 2026-09-15 and remains pending, as does HSR clearance. Expected close: by end of Q1 2027. WTRG's price is therefore substantially a merger-consideration price (0.305 × AWK, discounted for approval risk and time), not a standalone-DCF price.

## Owner's earnings
**FY2025 (10-K via EDGAR, from financials_history.csv):** operating cash flow $1,010,459,000; SBC $12,855,000 (always a real cost); capex $1,329,747,000 **by override** — the filed FY2025 figure is $1,429,980,000; see OVERRIDE.
- **Conservative owner's earnings FY2025: −$332,143,000 = −$1.18/share** (key_numbers.md). OCF does not cover the infrastructure program — that is structural for this business, not a bad year: OE-positive years in the last 5: **0/5**.
- Maintenance version (NI + D&A − min(capex, D&A) − ΔNWC): **+$307,321,000** for FY2025 (financials_history.csv). The two definitions diverge because the maintenance version charges only D&A ($417,471,000) as capex, while the company actually spent $1,429,980,000 (filed). For a manufacturer that gap would be growth capex; for a regulated utility it is rate-base investment that earns an allowed return only after rate cases catch up. The sweep's conservative definition is the scored one, and on it this company generates no owner's earnings — see SECTOR_MODEL_MISMATCH under Flags for what that does and doesn't mean.
- Net debt $8.097B (key_numbers.md; LongTermDebtNoncurrent + LongTermDebtCurrent basis), lease liabilities $28,271,000, equity $6,857,456,000 (FY2025, financials_history.csv). The capex gap is funded externally: FY2025 financing included $300,117,000 of at-the-market common-stock issuance and $567,448,000 of net commercial-paper proceeds (FY2025 10-K cash-flow statement), and the diluted share count compounds at +2.20%/yr (key_numbers.md share count CAGR) — steady dilution is part of the model.
- Dividends paid TTM $387,277,000 (fundamentals.json) are paid out of financing, not out of conservative OE.

**Base used = TTM owner's earnings through Q2 2026, from ttm.py (filing-direct):**
- OCF: FY $1,010,459,000 − prior YTD $571,834,000 + current YTD $588,980,000 = **TTM $1,027,605,000**
- Capex: **TTM $1,329,747,000**, all three legs filled by the override, prorated (see OVERRIDE)
- SBC: FY $12,855,000 − prior YTD $6,909,000 + current YTD $7,214,000 = **TTM $13,160,000**
- Shares (current-YTD weighted diluted): **283,998,000**
- **TTM OE total −$315,302,000 → base OE/share −$1.11** (base_source: ttm_json)
- The engine's normalized base (3-yr median) is −$1.52/share and the latest FY is −$1.18/share (key_numbers.md) — all three bases are negative, so the choice of base does not matter here. ## Moat: 5/10 — moderate; durable franchise, capped economics
Justification: exclusive regulated territories and essential-service demand make the franchise durable, but regulators cap the return on it: roic_proxy (fundamentals.json) ran 4.3% / 4.4% / 4.3% / 4.4% / 6.1% over FY2021–FY2025 — at or below a normal cost of capital — and gross margin is not filed (the company reports no COGS split, so no gross-margin series exists to quote). The moat protects volume and cost recovery, not price.
- FOR: exclusive regulated service territories — legal monopoly on water/wastewater for ~5.5 million people across nine states; essential, non-discretionary service with inelastic demand and a proven regulatory-recovery mechanism for infrastructure spend; rate-base model — the $1.7B 2026 infrastructure plan enters rate base and earns an allowed return, compounding regulated earnings; scale as one of the largest U.S. water/wastewater utilities, with a pipeline of municipal-system acquisitions.
- AGAINST: returns are set by regulators, not the company — allowed ROE caps the economics and ROIC has run only ~4–6%; capex structurally exceeds operating cash flow — growth is funded with debt and ATM equity issuance, diluting per-share economics; the gas segment faces long-run electrification/decarbonization transition risk; PFAS and water-quality mandates force capex whose recovery depends on rate-case outcomes; the pending American Water merger adds approval and integration risk, and the standalone moat is being absorbed into AWK's.
- A 5 gives CAP = 8.5 years (key_numbers.md): growth holds 2 years, then converges to the 2.5% terminal rate over 8.5 years. Moot for the verdict — there is no positive OE path to fade.

An OCF-minus-all-capex DCF structurally fails regulated utilities: capex is not discretionary maintenance, it is rate-base investment recovered through future rates, and the allowed return arrives over decades, funded meanwhile by debt and equity issuance. Confidence is **low** and the F should be read as "this model cannot value this business," not as "this business is worthless" — the maintenance-definition OE above (+$307,321,000 FY2025) and TTM net income of $554,870,000 show an accrual-profitable, dividend-paying regulated franchise. What the F does establish on the sweep's own terms: WTRG generates no conservative owner's earnings, so it cannot clear Andrew's 15% hurdle on this model, and no price fixes a negative base.

## My thoughts / overlay
- The standalone DCF question is about to be moot: if the AWK merger closes (expected by end of Q1 2027), WTRG holders will own 0.305 AWK shares per share and the analysis that matters is AWK's valuation and the remaining approval path (Pennsylvania, HSR), not WTRG's standalone cash flows. The $40.83 price should be benchmarked against 0.305 × AWK's price, not against any standalone IV — this model produces none.
- The structural cash story is real even if the tier overstates it: a decade of capex above OCF, net debt of $8.097B against $6.857B of equity, ~2.2%/yr share issuance, and a dividend paid from financing. Regulated utilities run this way by design — the return of and on that capital comes through rate cases, which is precisely the cash-flow timing an owner's-earnings DCF refuses to credit.
- Method range: conservative OE definition → F (this run). Maintenance definition (capex capped at D&A) → positive FY2025 OE of $307,321,000, which would support a conventional utility valuation — but that definition would flatter every capital-intensive grower in the sweep, so it is reported, not scored.

## Final verdict
- **Final tier: F** (no positive conservative owner's earnings; sub-type no_cash_generation; OE-positive years 0/5)
- Confidence: **Low** (SECTOR_MODEL_MISMATCH — the model structurally misfits regulated utilities; high confidence only in the narrow claim that conservative OE is negative)
- One-liner: Durable regulated water/gas monopoly (moat 5/10) whose capex structurally exceeds operating cash flow — conservative owner's earnings are negative in every recent year, so it cannot clear the 15% hurdle on this model at any plausible price; the live investment question is the pending all-stock American Water merger (0.305 AWK shares per WTRG share, expected to close by end of Q1 2027), not standalone DCF value.
